newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-DEVERS LIKELY TO RUN RELAY ONLY.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-DEVERS LIKELY TO RUN RELAY ONLY.

text.p: Gail Devers, granted a wild card card to the sixth world championships starting on Saturday as the defending high hurdles champion, is likely to run in the 4x100 metres relay only.
U.S. women's coach Gary Winckler said on Thursday Devers would anchor the relay team with American champion Marion Jones running the second leg.
"It is my information that she (Devers) will only run the relay," Winckler told a news conference.
Winckler said Jones would run second instead of anchoring the team because of Devers's experience. The 30-year-old American won the 1993 world 100 title and is the current Olympic champion.
"We feel Marion will help us better by running second," Winckler said.
Gwen Torrence, the defending 100 champion who also won a wild card, has pulled out of the championships.
U.S. men's champion Maurice Greene will anchor the men's relay team, who have lost to Canada both in the 1995 world championships and at last year's Atlanta Olympics.
Double Olympic champion Michael Johnson, another wild card selection, is one of a group of nine contesting a place in the 4x400 metres relay quartet.
"If he is going to run in the relay he's going to have to prove himself on the track," said head coach Dean Hayes.
"If he runs 43.5 I guess we are going to have to throw him in there."
